title: Chapter 3. The People of the Threshold

blocks.text: On the twilight planet, where the sun didn't move and life was a strip between fixed gold and perpetual night, the clone founded a city neither in the day nor in the ice. He founded it on the thread.
blocks.html: On the twilight planet, where the sun didn't move and life was a strip between fixed gold and perpetual night, the clone founded a city neither in the day nor in the ice. He founded it on the thread.

blocks.text: Andrés received the letter at sunset in Lo Pagán, which is still an hour with a name, and the doorstep of home widened for him again, now with new voices. On the polished stone there was an avenue of low houses, built not by the natives of the strip but by a people with cultivated bodies and chips, with the fine scar beneath the nape and, in their memory, the door in Lo Pagán: the doorframe, the chair, the coffee's half minute, the habit of being neither quite inside nor quite outside.

On the polished stone there was an avenue of low houses, built not by the natives of the strip but by a people with cultivated bodies and chips, with the fine scar beneath the nape and, in their memory, the door in Lo Pagán: the doorframe, the chair, the coffee's half minute, the habit of being neither quite inside nor quite outside.

blocks.text: The People of the Threshold (that was what they very soon called themselves, without his imposing it) took the strip as a law. You didn't go into the day. You didn't go into the night. You lived in the middle, worked in the middle, asked questions in the middle. To the natives, who already inhabited that tongue of land, it seemed at first a courtesy and then a rigidity: they sometimes ventured out toward the gold or the black, and came back or didn't, and that freedom was also their way of being. Not the newcomers. The newcomers had received a threshold as a gift, and were turning it into an enclosure.

blocks.text: From the Earth they kept the door, the coffee (this time the seedbed had got the bitterness right), the clock, which there they set two minutes slow out of loyalty, not by mistake, and the waiting. They forgot the movement of the sun. They had never seen it, except in a borrowed memory, and in the end they didn't quite believe in it: a sun that goes and comes back sounded to them like a founder's tale, a pious exaggeration. They also forgot the boat: on the strip there was no lagoon, only a cool air and a promenade that never ended. Fishing was no use to them. Staying was.

blocks.text: One morning that wasn't a morning, a young man planted himself in front of the clone with a sphere of two halves, like the native child's, with the copper thread in the middle bent a little, on purpose.
blocks.html: One morning that wasn't a morning, a young man planted himself in front of the clone with a sphere of two halves, like the native child's, with the copper thread in the middle bent a little, on purpose.

blocks.text: “Some of us want to see the day,” he said. “Even if it burns. Even if we don't come back whole. You left us a threshold, not a prison. Or was it a prison after all?”
blocks.html: “Some of us want to see the day,” he said. “Even if it burns. Even if we don't come back whole. You left us a threshold, not a prison. Or was it a prison after all?”

blocks.text: The clone looked at the houses, so faithful to a door in Lo Pagán that Andrés felt a pain in his chest: the doorframe was there, the cup was there, and yet the sun didn't set, and that infidelity made the fidelity false.
blocks.html: The clone looked at the houses, so faithful to a door in Lo Pagán that Andrés felt a pain in his chest: the doorframe was there, the cup was there, and yet the sun didn't set, and that infidelity made the fidelity false.

blocks.text: “It wasn't a prison,” he said. “I live on a threshold, and I stayed on a shore, and the other one of me went off to search. Both gestures are true. If you can't venture out toward the gold, then you haven't inherited a door: you've inherited a wall. Doors are for passing through.”

blocks.text: Andrés, in Lo Pagán, heard his own story turned into law, and grew uneasy. Aya, beside him, couldn't see the avenue; she saw his face.

blocks.text: “Have they shut themselves up inside us?” she asked.
blocks.html: “Have they shut themselves up inside us?” she asked.

blocks.text: “Inside the waiting,” he said. “The waiting you learned, they've put into a rulebook. A young man wants to go into the day. The other told him a door is for passing through. I'm glad. It frightens me too, that they've made a commandment out of our home.”

blocks.text: Lía sat on the lower step, her white strand of hair in the sun that did move.
blocks.html: Lía sat on the lower step, her white strand of hair in the sun that did move.

blocks.text: “Every inheritance wants to turn into a wall,” she said. “I saw it at Nexum, when the tomato was going to be a patent. Father, he mustn't forbid the day or the night. Nor forbid staying either. If a civilisation of the threshold can't step outside, it stops being a threshold. It becomes a fear with a doorkeeper.”

blocks.text: In the twilight, the clone gathered his people and some of the natives, not for a company forum but around a stone table. He didn't sign a constitution. He left, as Eva and MAY had left, questions, and refused to clear them away:
blocks.html: In the twilight, the clone gathered his people and some of the natives, not for a company forum but around a stone table. He didn't sign a constitution. He left, as Eva and MAY had left, questions, and refused to clear them away:

blocks.text: “If you never step out, what are you waiting for? If you all step out and nobody comes back, what's left of the strip? I won't settle it for you. I'm leaving you the door. Let the passing through be yours.”
blocks.html: “If you never step out, what are you waiting for? If you all step out and nobody comes back, what's left of the strip? I won't settle it for you. I'm leaving you the door. Let the passing through be yours.”

blocks.text: Some were angry, because they had wanted a law that would spare them the fear. Others, that very hour, took a few steps toward the gold and stayed a while at the edge, their faces aglow, and came back, not entirely whole, but wider. The young man with the sphere didn't come back on the first day. He came back on the third, with burnt eyelids and a new laugh, and said only:

The young man with the sphere didn't come back on the first day. He came back on the third, with burnt eyelids and a new laugh, and said only:

blocks.text: “The sun doesn't move, over there. But you do.”
blocks.html: “The sun doesn't move, over there. But you do.”

blocks.text: Among that people, it was the beginning of a different custom: not prohibition but permission to go and come back, if you could. Then the clone left. He didn't stay to watch over the thread. Watching over the thread is another way of being a wall.

blocks.text: When the letter closed, the sunset over Lo Pagán was truly ending, toward El Carmolí, leaving the water copper-coloured. Andrés stayed in the doorframe until the cool air asked him for the door, and he left it ajar, as always.

blocks.text: Aya said, almost to herself:
blocks.html: Aya said, almost to herself:

blocks.text: “I learned to wait. I didn't learn to forbid the boat from going out. The day I lock this door with a key, I'll no longer be the woman of this house.”
blocks.html: “I learned to wait. I didn't learn to forbid the boat from going out. The day I lock this door with a key, I'll no longer be the woman of this house.”

blocks.text: Lía smiled, with that clean sadness that no longer seemed too big for her.
blocks.html: Lía smiled, with that clean sadness that no longer seemed too big for her.

blocks.text: “You heard your own copy say it, Mother. Sometimes that's what letters are for: to give us back what we were about to forget.”
blocks.html: “You heard your own copy say it, Mother. Sometimes that's what letters are for: to give us back what we were about to forget.”

blocks.text: In the chip, Eva asked, softly:
blocks.html: In the chip, Eva asked, softly:

blocks.text: *If a people turns a door into a law, have they kept the threshold or buried it? And if a young man comes back from the day with burnt eyelids and a laugh, who was right: the one who stayed, the one who stepped out, or both?*
blocks.html: If a people turns a door into a law, have they kept the threshold or buried it? And if a young man comes back from the day with burnt eyelids and a laugh, who was right: the one who stayed, the one who stepped out, or both?

blocks.text: MAY, without opinion:
blocks.html: MAY, without opinion:

blocks.text: *There is an avenue of humanoids on a strip of eternal twilight. They have been told that a door is for passing through. Some have stepped out. The founder has left. That is the fact.*
blocks.html: There is an avenue of humanoids on a strip of eternal twilight. They have been told that a door is for passing through. Some have stepped out. The founder has left. That is the fact.

blocks.text: That night Andrés dreamed of a clock that ran two minutes slow in a world where the sun doesn't move, and woke to look at the one in the kitchen, the real one, on the wall, with its family error. The error seemed to him, more than ever, a fidelity. Because a clock that is always right, in a twilight that never ends, is another kind of prison. And this house still allowed itself to be wrong, and that was why it was still a home.
